claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Yes, I have one child - Alex. He's 18 and still living at home with me. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can see you have one child, Alex, who is 18 and living at home with you.

Since Alex is 18, a key factor for Child Benefit eligibility is whether he's in approved education or training. Child Benefit can continue for young people aged 16-19 if they're in approved education or training.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training (such as A-levels, T-levels, NVQ Level 3 or below, or similar qualifications)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is! Alex is doing his A-levels at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great! Since Alex is 18, still living at home with you, and is doing his A-levels (which counts as approved education), this is very positive for your eligibility.

Now I need to understand a bit more about your circumstances:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent. Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Are you currently responsible for Alex - meaning you live with him and/or contribute to his upkeep (such as food, clothes, or pocket money)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. He lives with me and I'm responsible for him - I cover all his food, clothes, and everything he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for confirming that.

One more important question:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

- **Alex's age and education**: Although Alex is 18, you can still claim Child Benefit because he's in approved education (A-levels). Child Benefit can continue for young people under 20 who stay in approved education or training.

- **Your responsibility**: You live with Alex and are responsible for all his upkeep, which satisfies the responsibility requirement.

- **UK residence**: You live in the UK, which meets the residency requirement.

- **No other claimant**: Nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex, so there's no conflict.

**Important things to note:**

- Child Benefit will continue as long as Alex remains in approved education and is under 20 years old.
- If Alex leaves education, starts working 24 hours or more per week, or starts claiming certain benefits in his own right, you should inform HMRC as this would affect your Child Benefit.
- If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge.

If you haven't already claimed, you can apply for Child Benefit. If you have any other questions, feel free to ask!
